text:
maria: Heads-up — our hosted demand forecast just jumped for the next 7 days, looks like we could hit a GPU shortfall if trends continue. attaching quick numbers / proposal. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

jon: How big is the shift? any particular region or model family driving it?

maria: Primary driver: embeds + short-chat traffic in us-west1 and eu-west1. 24h change: +28% embed tokens, peak hour GPU-hours up ~34%.

sam: Do we have a concrete gap estimate?

maria: Rough calc from last 24h baseline + forecasted growth: committed pool = 1120 GPUs across hosted; expected peak demand = ~1420 GPUs -> gap ~300 GPUs (range 250-420 depending on SLO headroom). this assumes current batching & caching stays same.

kevin: If that's accurate we need cost/commitment runbook. lead time to add reserved capacity from cloud partner?

maria: From procurement notes: 7-14 days to finalize placement + billing, but that doesn't guarantee hardware availability in the region.

jon: Short-term mitigations?

sam: Ideas: 1) route lower-priority embed/bulk requests to eu-central or to quantized model variants; 2) temporarily reduce background batch index jobs; 3) enable cross-region spillover for hosted API when us-west1 saturated.

maria: +1. Also we can drop noncritical default batch window from 6h to 2h to shave ~30-50 GPU-hours/day.

kevin: Any billing anomalies that could explain a phantom consumption spike (e.g., mis-tagged jobs)? we should rule out leakage before buying more.

maria: Good call — I ran a quick tag audit, see snippet below:

```
SELECT region, sum(gpu_hours) as gpu_hours, count(distinct instance_id) as hosts
FROM billing.gpu_usage
WHERE ts >= date_sub(current_date(), interval 7 day)
GROUP BY region;
```

maria: Results looked consistent: us-west1 + eu-west1 are both up. no single mis-tagged job dominating.

ops-bot: autoscaler snapshot: committed_capacity_us_west1=480, committed_capacity_eu_west1=320, burst_credit_us_west1=120, active_reserved=1120

jon: If we enable spillover, what's the networking/latency impact for chat endpoints?

sam: For small interactive chat it's risky (p95 latency up 40-80ms cross-region). For embeddings and async endpoints it's fine. we should only spillover embed and batch-generation routes.

kevin: If we buy short-term reserved capacity elsewhere, can we shift billing to meet commitments without breaking enterprise SLAs? procurement needs clear commit vs spot mix.

maria: Proposal: immediate 72h plan:
- Enable routing policy: spillover embed->eu-central, batch->alternate pools (owner: sam)
- Temporarily throttle noncritical batch jobs by 25% (owner: jon)
- Open capacity request with cloud partner for +320 GPUs in us-west1 and us-east1 (owner: maria)
- Finance to review commit tradeoffs if partner offers 30/60 day commitments (owner: kevin)

jon: I'll roll the routing change as a feature flag gated by traffic threshold. quick PR incoming.

sam: I'll do batch throttling and surface expected GPU-hours saved in 6h.

kevin: I'll model the math for 30 vs 90 day commits and run ROI per GPU-hour at our current unit price.

maria: Also opening support ticket with cloud: https://cloud.vendor/support/tickets/INC-98321 — asked them for short-term capacity hold and pricing for 30/60 day commitments.

support-bot: Ticket INC-98321 created, priority P2. expected response window 4h.

jon: Any risk to Hosted SLAs? need to notify customers or ramp down lower tiers first.

maria: Plan is to avoid SLA impact by confining throttles to internal batch/ingest routes and non-enterprise customers if needed. we'll update status page only if we see error spikes.

kevin: Sounds good — please post an update in 6h with measured savings and cloud response.

maria: Will do. thanks team. :pray:
